- Expected peak TPS (calls per second) during your busiest hour. 
- P95 latency SLO for end-user requests (e.g., 300ms p95, 800ms p95, etc.).

How we'll use that: I'll translate into tokens/sec (avg tokens * TPS) and then map to our SKU matrix (v100-equivalent, a10x2, q4-8 quant) to show committed capacity, expected p95 tail with KV cache assumptions, and recommended headroom percentage for burst tolerance.

I sketched a few conservative scenarios in the attached helios_compute_matrix_v1.xlsx — don't worry about the numbers yet; I'll refine once you send the three inputs.

Next steps

- If you want, we can schedule a 30-min follow-up to walk the SKU trade-offs.

Hi Sergio, thanks — quick answers below. We tried to keep the ask tight so procurement can see a few lanes.

- Avg tokens per call: 420 tokens (includes user prompt + assistant reply).
- Expected peak TPS (calls/sec): 2.8 calls/sec during peak hour (we currently throttle to that internally but expect spikes).
- P95 latency SLO: 450ms p95 is the target we want to meet for API-to-user perceived latency.

A few other notes that matter for modeling:
- We run a fair bit of context reuse (same conversation threads reused) so KV caching should help 30–40% of calls for longer sequences.
- We expect a staged rollout: pilot (Q3) at ~10% of peak, then ramp to full commit by Q1 next year.
- Procurement asked for both committed capacity and a conservative burst plan that doesn’t blow the monthly token budget.

If you can translate to tokens/sec and show a 10/20/30% headroom matrix across SKU mixes that would be ideal.

Looping Rachel in for ops math and to propose SKU mixes. Based on Taylor's numbers I ran a quick back-of-envelope:

Raw calc: avg tokens per call * TPS = tokens/sec
420 tokens * 2.8 calls/sec = 1,176 tokens/sec

Peak tokens/sec (with 30% burst headroom) = 1,529 tokens/sec

Assumptions I used:
- Baseline model = 7B dense-sized variant (our q4_8 runtime).
- Effective per-GPU throughput: q4_8 on a8x2 equiv -> ~4k tokens/sec sustained (single GPU equivalence with batching and prefix cache warm).
- Cold-cache penalty: first 30s of traffic to a new shard increases per-token latency by ~2.2x. Caching 40% of calls reduces effective load by that proportion for sustained periods.

Proposed SKU mixes (starter):
- Conservative commit (small): reserve 1 x a8x2 pool (equiv ~4k t/s) -> covers baseline + 160% headroom at cost X. Good for pilots and safety.
- Balanced commit: reserve 0.5 x v100-equivalent (older preemptible style) + 0.5 x a8x2 -> combinational throughput ~3.2k t/s with better cost efficiency if they accept slightly higher tail latency.
- Aggressive commit (SLA-grade): reserve 1 x a8x2 + hot-burst pool (burst on-demand) to ensure p95 hit with cold-cache churn.

Rachel — can you take the numbers and produce a simple matrix (tokens/sec -> required GPUs by SKU for 0%, 10%, 20%, 30% headroom) and estimate p95 margin under our cache assumptions? If you can attach an export (xlsx) I’ll drop it in the HubSpot deal.

Ben
Lead Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>

Hi all — attached is the matrix and two quick scenario exports: token_profile_samples.csv (sample traffic profile) and helios_compute_matrix_v1.xlsx (SKU mix + GPUs required). Key outputs and takeaway summary below.

Summary (short):
- Nominal tokens/sec (from Helio): 1,176 t/s; apply 30% headroom -> 1,529 t/s target capacity for safety.
- Recommended reserved SKU for committed contract: 1 x a8x2-equivalent slab (covers 4k t/s nominal) — this gives ~160% headroom relative to target and leaves room for other background workloads.
- Cost-efficient option (if Helio wants to minimize commit): 0.5 a8x2 + 0.5 v100-equivalent = ~3.2k t/s combined; expect p95 to be ~1.1x baseline due to inter-SKU variance and cold-cache on v100 lanes. Suitable if Helio accepts slightly higher latency tail.
- Burst plan: enable autoscale-on-demand for an additional 0.5 a8x2 equivalence for short windows (keeps monthly committed spend low while meeting p95 in spikes).

P95 modeling notes:
- With KV cache hit rate 40% and batching optimized for their 420-token average, our simulated p95 for the aggressive SKU (1 x a8x2 reserved) is ~380–420ms — within their 450ms target with modest safety margin.
- If cache hit rate drops below 25% (heavy cold-context churn), p95 can slip to ~550–650ms on the balanced commit; this is where burst-on-demand helps.

Attachments:
- helios_compute_matrix_v1.xlsx (breaks down required GPUs per tokens/sec step, cost delta per month by SKU mix)
- token_profile_samples.csv (10-minute synthetic sample we used to run the latency model)

Next steps/checklist:
- Taylor: confirm whether procurement wants committed commit-only lanes or a smaller commit + burst-on-demand.
- Sergio: I can prepare a formal commitment/spec sheet with explicit unit economics (monthly token budget vs slab cost + burst units) once procurement confirms preference.
- We suggest a 30-min walkthrough with Helio procurement + engineering next Tue; propose 10:00am PT.

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Solutions Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.ai
